assessment.rationale: Real-time spoken translation through earbuds is shipped, but only for tens of languages and only to smartphone owners, so the Main KPI of 8,000,000,000 people with real-time translation of any spoken language is unmet. Google Translate live translate works with any headphones in over 70 languages (https://www.techradar.com/computing/software/google-smashes-language-barriers-with-live-translation-for-any-earbuds-on-android-heres-how-it-works); AirPods Live Translation covers about nine languages on recent iPhones (https://www.which.co.uk/news/article/we-tested-apples-live-translation-feature-does-it-really-work-aClEt6o0zOut); Meta SeamlessStreaming is open for non-commercial use with about 100 input and 36 speech output languages (https://tech.slator.com/?p=93562). Speech recognition itself reaches only 1,600 of more than 7,000 languages even in Meta's open Omnilingual ASR (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.09690). Honest limit: earpiece translation among the major 70 to 100 languages is a known answer; only long-tail languages, offline low-cost devices for people without smartphones, and measured quality are open work.

additionalSearches.finding: AirPods Live Translation supports about nine languages and needs an iPhone 15 Pro or later with Apple Intelligence.

additionalSearches.finding: SeamlessStreaming: near-real-time translation, nearly 100 input languages, 36 speech output languages; released for non-commercial use.

additionalSearches.query: number of languages supported speech translation 7000 languages low-resource gap Omnilingual ASR
additionalSearches.finding: Omnilingual ASR (Apache 2.0) covers over 1,600 languages; most of the 7,000+ languages remain unsupported.

additionalSearches.finding: Google live translate (Dec 2025 beta, iOS 2026) works with any headphones and over 70 languages.
